title: mixed-workload-slo-simulation-suite-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview
--------
This document describes the "Mixed Workload SLO Simulation Suite": a standardized harness and set of templates for exercising the Redwood serving runtime with realistic, mixed request profiles to validate SLO compliance, scheduling behavior, and cost/latency tradeoffs. The goal is to provide reproducible simulations that approximate production mixes (chat + single-turn generation + embeddings + reranking) and to produce actionable artifacts: heatmaps, kernel utilization traces, SLO compliance reports, and recommended tuning knobs.

Why we need a mixed-workload simulator
-------------------------------------
- Synthetic single-pattern microbenchmarks (e.g., pure seq2seq or single-batch throughput) do not capture interference effects (KV cache pressure, kernel mixing, batching variability).
- Many incidents and surprises come from workload composition: long-sequence chat requests interleaved with short-embedding traffic can create scheduling pathologies.
- The suite provides a shared canonical set of mixes for perf regression testing, capacity planning, and release gating.

Scope and audience
------------------
This doc is for SREs, runtime engineers, and benchmark owners who:
- Need to validate that changes to kernel scheduling, batching, or memory management do not regress SLOs.
- Are preparing model-onboarding or kernel updates that must be evaluated under production-like mixes.
- Own capacity planning spreadsheets and want simulated unit economics under different quotas.

Simulator components and responsibilities
----------------------------------------
- simulator-cli (service-local binary): orchestrates request injection, sampling, and metrics export (Prometheus format).
- workload-templates: set of YAML files that encode arrival processes, token distributions, model variants, and error profiles.
- collector: lightweight process that aggregates kernel traces (ftrace / NVTX), per-request latencies, and GPU utilization into a single results bundle.
- report-generator: converts raw traces into SLO compliance reports, heatmaps, and recommended config deltas.

Canonical workload templates (included)
-------------------------------------
1) interactive-chat-heavy.yaml
   - mix: 60% chat (avg 120 tokens, multi-turn), 20% short generation (avg 24 tokens), 15% embeddings, 5% rerank
   - arrival distribution: bursty Poisson with peak factor 6x
2) embedding-bursty.yaml
   - mix: 70% embeddings (batched), 20% short generation, 10% control-plane ops
   - arrival distribution: steady with periodic spikes (TTL 30s)
3) enterprise-mixed.yaml
   - mix: 40% chat, 30% long generation (avg 512 tokens), 20% embeddings, 10% admin calls
   - includes auth token exchange latency emulation (50-200 ms)

SLOs used for simulation and gates
---------------------------------
Below are the canonical SLO thresholds used by the harness when flagging regressions. These reflect Redwood product SLO framing for shared-hosted capacity tests; dedicated/private gating may use stricter or alternate percentiles.

| class | p50 | p95 | p99 | success-rate | notes |
| chat (interactive) | "<=30ms/token" | "<=80ms/token" | "<=250ms/token" | >=99.5% | measured per-token after initial 128 tokens |
| short-gen | <=20ms/token | <=60ms/token | <=200ms/token | >=99.8% | includes continuous batching variance |
| embeddings (batched) | N/A | <=120ms (batch) | <=300ms (batch) | >=99.9% | batch-size distribution reported |
| control-plane | <=150ms | <=500ms | <=2s | >=99% | includes auth and routing checks |

(If the table renders poorly in plain text, the harness emits the same thresholds as JSON in results/assertions.json.)

Simulation procedure (recommended run)
-------------------------------------
1. Environment setup
   - Ensure test cluster uses the runtime image tag: runtime-e2e:staging-2026-01.
   - Reserve a node-pool labeled "bench/purpose=sim" with the same GPU family as the target fleet (A100 or H100).
   - Start collector: ./collector --out results/$(date -Iseconds)-bundle.tar
2. Kick off simulator
   - Example command: ./simulator-cli run --template=interactive-chat-heavy.yaml --duration=30m --concurrency=200 --export=results/run-01
3. Live monitoring
   - Metrics: simulator exports prometheus metrics at :9091/metrics. Watch these grafana panels: runtime/latency-by-model, kernel/occupancy, kvcache/hit-ratio
4. Trace capture
   - Enable NVTX on runtime for this run (ENV: RUNTIME_NVTX=1). Collector will grab NVTX spans and attach to each request id.
5. Post-processing
   - ./report-generator --input results/run-01 --assertions assertions.json --output reports/run-01-report.zip
6. Review failing assertions and heatmaps.

Typical outputs and artifacts
----------------------------
- reports/run-01-report.zip: includes per-request CSV, per-kernel timeline SVGs, occupancy heatmaps, and assertions.json.
- results/raw-traces.tar: NVTX + ftrace snippets keyed by request id.
- SLO compliance dashboard: automatic upload to internal dashboard at /dashboards/slo-simulations (requires internal VPN).

Interpreting common failure modes
--------------------------------
- Elevated p99 for chat with low average GPU utilization: suggests batching misalignment (high variance in sequence lengths). Actions: review batch-orchestrator logs, enable length-aware batching key, or reduce max-batch-latency-ms by 5ms and re-run.
- High embedding latency variance during busy windows: check data-plane prefetch/backpressure and embedding-service connectors. Consider increasing embed-batcher pool size.
- Kernel thrashing (many short kernels executed per request) correlating with CPU interrupt spikes: run kernel-scheduler sampling with --sample-interval=50ms and attach kernel-telemetry logs to the incident.

Recommended knobs and guardrails (quick checklist)
-------------------------------------------------
- batch-orchestrator.max_batch_latency_ms: default 12 (reduce to 8 for low-latency workloads).
- kernel-scheduler.priority_map: map interactive chat -> high, embeddings -> medium, batch-inference -> low.
- kv-cache.size_threshold_mb: 2048 (monitor for eviction spikes).
- runtime.gpu_compute_mode: exclusive_process for Dedicated, default for Hosted.

Sample config YAML (simulation override)
-------------------------------------
simulation_overrides:
  concurrency: 200
  arrival_jitter: 0.15
  enable_nvtx: true
  batch_overrides:
    max_latency_ms: 8
    dynamic_by_length: true

Example CLI snippet to compare two build images (A/B run)
------------------------------------------------------
# Run baseline
./simulator-cli run --template=enterprise-mixed.yaml --duration=45m --image runtime-e2e:staging-2026-01 --export=results/baseline
# Run candidate
./simulator-cli run --template=enterprise-mixed.yaml --duration=45m --image runtime-e2e:candidate-2026-02 --export=results/candidate
# Produce diff report
./report-generator --compare results/baseline results/candidate --output reports/diff-2026-02.zip

Acceptance criteria for CI gating
--------------------------------
- Candidate must not have >0.3% additional p99 violations for any class compared to baseline for the canonical templates.
- GPU compute cost (tokens-per-dollar) regression must be < 4%.
- No new kernel-level OOM traces or >2% increase in kv-cache eviction rate.

Ownership and run cadence
-------------------------
- Benchmark harness owner: perf-eng team (contact: perf-eng@redwood.com).
- Runtime SLO steward: Priya Narang (runtime-slo@redwood.com).
- Recommended cadence: run full suite weekly; run critical templates on every release candidate.

Telemetry and dashboards
------------------------
- Exported metrics (Prometheus): simulator.request_latency_ms_bucket, simulator.request_success_total, kernel.occupancy_pct, gpu.utilization_pct, kvcache.hit_ratio.
- Dashboards: perf/slo-simulations (auto-upload), runtime/kernel-telemetry (manual attach).

Troubleshooting checklist (quick)
--------------------------------
1. Noisy baseline: verify collector was not running with debug NVTX (this inflates latency).
2. Missing traces: check RUNTIME_NVTX env and kernel build flags.
3. Non-deterministic failures: re-run with fixed random seed: --seed=42.

How to add a new template
-------------------------
1. Create YAML under workloads/ with descriptive name and include: summary, arrival_profile, model_map, token_distribution, error_profile.
2. Add an entry in templates/index.yaml with owner and linked PR.
3. Run the template locally for 30m and submit results to perf-eng for review.

Security and data hygiene
-------------------------
- The harness must not use real customer data. Use sanitized prompt sets (stored in /data/sanitized-prompts).
- Uploads to the shared dashboard must strip auth tokens and customer identifiers. The report-generator will redact any headers matching Authorization|X-Customer-ID.

Appendix: example assertions.json snippet
--------------------------------------
{
  "assertions": [
    {
      "name": "chat_p99",
      "threshold": 250,
      "unit": "ms_per_token",
      "op": "<="
    }
  ]
}
